7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda: Price & Calories

A medium Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda is about $3.50, with 250 calories, 0 mg of caffeine and 63 g of sugar. Every number here comes from 7 Brew's own published nutrition guide, broken out by size and preparation.

Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda allergens

7 Brew's published allergen guide lists no declared allergens for the standard Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda. Adding a milk, syrup or topping changes this, and every drink is made on shared equipment, so cross-contact is possible.

If you are ordering around an allergy, check the full allergen and dietary guide and confirm at the window.

How to order a Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda

Ask for it by name — it is on the standard board at every 7 Brew, so no special script is needed. Say the size first, then the drink: "Can I get a medium Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda?"

Worth knowing before you order: the base is customisable. You can swap milk, ask for sugar-free syrups, change the sweetness level, or have most drinks made iced, hot or blended as a frozen chiller where the menu allows. Ordering through the app earns 100 rewards points either way.

Make a Blood Orange Fizz at Home

Two syrups and sparkling water. The only trick is balance: orange brings the sweet citrus, pomegranate brings the tart, and they go in evenly.

For one medium fizz

  • 1/2 oz orange syrup
  • 1/2 oz pomegranate syrup
  • 10 to 12 oz plain sparkling water
  • A full cup of ice
  • Optional: a splash of cream for the orange-cream version
  1. Both syrups over the ice.
  2. Sparkling water in slow, then one gentle stir.
  3. Taste before you add anything. It should bite a little. That is the point of this one.

Going bigger or sweeter? Fan recipes for a large, extra-sweet build use a full ounce of each syrup. That tracks: the syrup amount roughly doubles with the cup. Energy version at home: same syrups over a can of energy drink instead of sparkling water. That is a different drink with caffeine, so label your pitcher if both are in the fridge.

7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda FAQ

How many calories are in a 7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda?

A medium iced Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda has 250 calories. A small has 170 and a large 340, according to 7 Brew's nutrition guide.

How much caffeine is in a 7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda?

0 mg. The fizz line is caffeine free at every size, kids included.

How much does a 7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda cost?

Roughly $2.75 for a small, $3.50 for a medium and $4.25 for a large. Prices are our estimates and vary by stand — every 7 Brew is independently owned.

How much sugar is in a 7 Brew Blood Orange 7 Fizz Soda?

63 g in a medium.

Is there really a blood orange in it, or a blood orange syrup?

Neither. There is no blood orange syrup on the 7 Brew board. The drink is orange syrup plus pomegranate syrup in sparkling water, and the mix lands on that deep red-orange color and tart bite the name promises. 7 Brew says it right on the menu: orange and pomegranate, for a tart citrus bite. One of the top guides online never figures this out and lists a blood orange flavored syrup as the ingredient. There is not one.

Is the Blood Orange Fizz the same as a Blood Orange Energy?

Same flavors, different drink. This page is the fizz: sparkling water base, zero caffeine, 250 calories in a medium. The same orange and pomegranate combo can be ordered on the 7 Energy base, and plenty of people do, which is why searches for blood orange energy are everywhere. If you want the taste without the buzz, order the fizz and say the word fizz out loud. The names are close enough that cups get mixed up.

Why do other sites list 80 calories, or 435, for this drink?

Because the fizz numbers online are a mess. One top guide puts a medium at about 435 calories, another says 150 to 220, a third says 80 to 150. The official nutrition guide says 250 calories and 63 g of sugar for a medium iced, with 170 in a small and 340 in a large. Those are the numbers in the table above, and they are the ones to plan around.

Should I add cream to a Blood Orange Fizz?

If you like an orange cream soda, yes. The default build is clear and bubbly, nothing creamy in it. Cream, whipped cream and cold foam are all official toppings on this drink, and a light splash of cream softens the tart edge into something that tastes like the orange creamsicles from the ice cream truck. Fans figured this out a while ago. It is the most common upgrade on this flavor.

Is there a sugar-free Blood Orange Fizz?

Not as a published drink. The official guide has no sugar-free Blood Orange entry, so there are no official numbers for one. Both syrups do exist in sugar-free form, and the official page lists sugar-free flavor options for this drink, so many stands can build it if you ask. Just know any calorie number attached to it would be a guess. Half sweet or quarter sweet is the route with predictable sugar, and the tartness carries the drink fine at half. The drinks that do come sugar-free, all 43 of them, are compared on our sugar-free page.

How is Blood Orange different from Pixie Stick?

One syrup. Blood Orange is orange and pomegranate. Add almond to that pair and you have the Pixie Stick flavor, the candy one from the Pixie Stick drinks. If Blood Orange tastes like a tart citrus soda, Pixie Stick tastes like the same soda walked through a candy aisle. Order back to back sometime. The almond is doing more work than you would expect.
